original_query: SELECT t6.JOB, CAST(t6.EXPR1 * t7.f1 AS INTEGER) FROM (SELECT JOB, SUM(SAL) AS EXPR1 FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A' GROUP BY JOB) AS t6 INNER JOIN (SELECT NAME, COUNT(*) AS f1 FROM DEPT GROUP BY NAME) AS t7 ON t6.JOB = t7.NAME
rewritten_query:
SELECT e.JOB, CAST(SUM(e.SAL) AS INTEGER) AS EXPR1
FROM EMP e
JOIN DEPT d ON d.NAME = e.JOB
WHERE e.ENAME = 'A'
GROUP BY e.JOB;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Flatten the two derived tables (t6, t7) into a direct join between EMP and DEPT, applying the selective filter ENAME='A' before aggregation and performing a single GROUP BY at the end (join-then-aggregate).

The rewritten form is semantically equivalent: joining filtered EMP rows to DEPT duplicates each EMP row by the number of matching DEPT rows (COUNT per NAME), so SUM(e.SAL) after the join equals the original t6.EXPR1 * t7.f1. This removes the full DEPT pre-aggregation and one join stage.
Push the highly selective filter ENAME='A' into the FROM/JOIN stage so that only ~99 filtered EMP rows participate in the join and aggregation.
